cards.text: Chronicles has been tracing Israel's family tree tribe by tribe (1 Chronicles 2 through 5), and now it's Levi's turn, starting with his sons Gershon, Kohath and Merari. From Kohath's son Amram come Aaron, whom God set apart to serve as priest (Exodus 28:1), Moses, Israel's leader, and their sister Miriam the prophetess (Exodus 15:20). One house gave Israel a priest, a leader AND a prophetess, and I can't get one batch out of the oven without burning a corner.

From Aaron's son Eleazar, the family line runs father to son, through names like Phinehas and Zadok, and an Azariah who served as priest in the temple that Solomon, king of Israel (1 Kings 4:1), built in Jerusalem. It ends with Jehozadak, who went into captivity when the LORD sent Judah and Jerusalem into exile by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon (2 Kings 25:1).

Then comes the clan list: Gershom, Kohath and Merari, each with his family down the line, and Kohath's line has an Elkanah, then another Elkanah, then ANOTHER Elkanah. Friend, if you yell 'Elkanah!' at that family reunion, you'd better say which one. Then come Joel and Abijah, the sons of Samuel, the prophet who anointed David, Israel's future king (1 Samuel 8:2, 16:13).

cards.question: After the ark rested in the house of the LORD, David put a group of Levites in charge of the ___ there.

cards.text: These men are singing before Solomon ever builds the house of the LORD in Jerusalem. I sang to my oven once, friend, and the timer went off EARLY just to drown me out.

cards.question: Until Solomon built the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, David's singers ministered with song before the ___.
How did David's singers carry out their duties before the tabernacle?

answers.text: According to the regulations given them
Only when the king was there

cards.text: Now we meet the singers who served, together with their sons. Heman the singer is from Kohath's clan, and his line climbs back through Samuel all the way to Levi, the son of Israel. His kinsman Asaph, from Gershom's clan, served at his right hand, and on the left were their kinsmen the sons of Merari, starting with Ethan. Three clans, one choir.

cards.question: Besides the singers, what were the other Levites assigned to?

answers.text: Every kind of service of the tabernacle
Guarding the gates of the king's palace
Collecting the taxes from every tribe

cards.question: True or false: The other Levites shared the work of the Most Holy Place with Aaron and his sons.
Aaron and his sons present offerings on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense. What are the offerings for?

answers.text: To ask for rain on the land

cards.question: True or false: Aaron and his sons did their work according to all that Moses the servant of God had commanded.

cards.text: Then Aaron's line is listed again, down to Zadok and his son Ahimaaz. After that, the Levites are given territories to settle in, and Aaron's descendants from Kohath's clan come first.

cards.question: Aaron's descendants come first when the Levites are given their territories. Why them first?

answers.text: The first lot fell to them

cards.text: Aaron's descendants get Hebron, a city of refuge, with its pasturelands, but the fields and villages around the city go to Caleb son of Jephunneh, one of the men Moses sent to scout the land (Numbers 13:3, 6). Then the rest of the Kohathites, the Gershomites and the Merarites get towns from tribe after tribe, so the Levites end up with towns on both sides of the Jordan. Shechem in Ephraim's hill country is a city of refuge too. Take it from a guy who lived years in the back of a junk drawer: a place to call home is a BIG deal.
